content.value_statement: Complex TypeScript features can create unclear APIs and slow feedback. This skill provides structured patterns for types, guards, configuration, and type-safe application design.
actual_capabilities: Design branded types, discriminated unions, and generic type utilities.
Create type guards and assertion functions for safe narrowing.
Recommend strict TypeScript compiler settings and project references.
Explain mapped, conditional, and template literal types.
Provide patterns for type-safe API clients and state machines.
Suggest declaration file and incremental compilation settings.
limitations: Does not run TypeScript compilers or modify project files by itself.
Does not replace project-specific architecture review or testing.
Examples require adaptation for the project framework and TypeScript version.
Does not validate external API contracts at runtime.

use_cases.title: Strengthen a TypeScript domain model
use_cases.description: Create branded identifiers and discriminated states that prevent common data mix-ups.

use_cases.title: Configure a strict monorepo
use_cases.description: Plan project references, path mappings, and incremental builds for multiple packages.

use_cases.title: Design typed API boundaries
use_cases.description: Define request and response types, guards, and error results for reliable client code.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: add strict settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tsconfig and recommend strict compiler options. Explain each change in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: model domain IDs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create branded TypeScript types for UserId and OrderId. Show safe constructors and usage examples.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: build a type guard
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a type guard for this unknown API response. Include a discriminated union and clear failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: improve monorepo types
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose TypeScript project references, path mappings, and build settings for this multi-package repository. Identify tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Create a safe state model for a request that can load, succeed, or fail.
output: A discriminated union for each request state.
An exhaustive rendering strategy that catches unhandled states.
A short explanation of how narrowing prevents invalid property access.

output_examples.input: Review my compiler configuration for a published library.
output: Recommended strict compiler options and declaration settings.
Notes about module resolution and compatibility.
A prioritized checklist for validating the build.

output_examples.input: Define a reusable utility type for nested readonly data.
output: Usage guidance for nested objects and arrays.
Warnings about compiler performance on deeply nested types.

best_practices: Enable strict compiler settings before adding advanced type abstractions.
Validate untrusted runtime data with type guards because TypeScript types are erased.
Keep public API types explicit and test important type contracts.
anti_patterns: Do not use any or broad assertions to silence type errors without documenting the reason.
Do not treat compile-time types as runtime validation for external input.
Do not introduce deeply recursive types without checking compiler performance.

faq.question: What TypeScript versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on TypeScript 5.0 and later features, but patterns may need adaptation for older versions.

faq.question: Can this skill validate API data at runtime?
faq.answer: It can propose type guards and validation patterns, but the application must execute the validation.

faq.question: Does it configure tRPC?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for end-to-end type safety and tRPC-related design, not automated installation or deployment.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing tsconfig file?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the configuration and project context for targeted recommendations.

faq.question: Will it remove all TypeScript errors?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest fixes, but project code, dependencies, and tests require separate verification.

faq.question: Is this useful for JavaScript projects?
faq.answer: It is designed for TypeScript. Some configuration and API-design guidance may apply after a JavaScript project adopts TypeScript.
